short: Parallel decoder, learned-feature GAN generator and transformer front end (M06) are standard; 9.14x mel speedup is real, but evaluation (M12) drops the STOI/ESTOI its Lip2Wav baseline reported.
position: FastLTS [@wang2022fastlts] changes one component, the decoding path (M06): a parallel acoustic decoder, a GAN generator fed with learned features instead of mel spectrograms, and a spatial-temporal transformer front end. All three are standard: direct waveform generation predates it [@mira2021endtoend], and so does a transformer visual front end for lip reading [@prajwal2021vtp]. The speedup is real but partly misattributed: 9.14× at the mel level is the non-autoregressive effect, while the 19.76× waveform figure mostly replaces Griffin-Lim with a GAN vocoder (§5.5), and no parallel mel-plus-vocoder system is timed. Evaluation (M12) is behind its own baseline: it drops the STOI/ESTOI that Lip2Wav reported on the same three speakers [@prajwal2020learning], and its Table 1 shows lower intelligibility than Lip2Wav on Chemistry Lectures.
